Add `scripts/cleanup_old_vultr_test_instances.py`, an out-of-band, age-based reaper for Vultr VPS instances left behind by the mngr_vultr release tests (e.g. when a test session is killed before its in-process cleanup runs). It destroys instances whose `mngr-vultr-test-created` tag is older than `--max-age-hours` (default 1.0) and no-ops if `VULTR_API_KEY` is unset. Wired into CI as a `cleanup-vultr-instances` job mirroring the existing `cleanup-modal-environments` job.

Correct the docstrings of `scripts/cleanup_old_vultr_test_instances.py` and `scripts/cleanup_old_modal_test_environments.py`, and the `cleanup-vultr-instances` CI job comment, which previously described the cleanup as running "periodically" / "on a schedule" / "hourly". There is no cron trigger; these CI cleanup jobs run on every push to main and every pull request. The docstrings now say so.

Extend the same out-of-band, age-based reaper pattern to the other cloud providers. Add `scripts/cleanup_old_aws_test_instances.py`, `scripts/cleanup_old_gcp_test_instances.py`, and `scripts/cleanup_old_azure_test_instances.py`, each destroying test instances tagged/labeled `mngr-pytest-launched=true` that are older than `--max-age-hours` (default 1.0), and each no-ops when its provider credentials cannot be resolved. Wired into CI as `cleanup-aws-instances`, `cleanup-gcp-instances`, and `cleanup-azure-instances` jobs alongside the existing Modal and Vultr cleanup jobs. The AWS job uses the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` secrets already present in CI; the GCP and Azure jobs are safe no-ops until their respective secrets are configured.

All four provider scripts (and each provider's session-end leak detector) now share a single reaper implementation in `imbue.mngr_vps.leak_cleanup` rather than four per-provider copies; each script just builds its provider's VPS client and calls the shared scan/destroy.

The Vultr, AWS, and GCP cleanup jobs fetch their credentials from Vault (`mngr/ci/VULTR_API_KEY`, `mngr/ci/AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `mngr/ci/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `mngr/ci/GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY`) via the `use-vault-secrets` action (GitHub OIDC, role `mngr_ci_gh`) rather than GitHub Actions secrets, matching the repo's secret-storage policy. The GCP service-account key JSON is stored base64-encoded because GitHub's log masking is line-based and exact-match, so a raw multi-line JSON secret would leak into CI logs; the job decodes it when materializing `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. The Azure job remains a safe no-op until its account is provisioned and its credentials land under `mngr/ci/`.

Correct the docstrings of `scripts/cleanup_old_aws_test_instances.py` and `scripts/cleanup_old_gcp_test_instances.py`, which described the age check as reading EC2 `LaunchTime` / GCE `creation_timestamp`. The shared reaper actually reads the `mngr-created-at` tag (AWS) / instance metadata (GCP) that each provider's `create_instance` stamps. No behavior change.
